title: SummitCare - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for SummitCare onboarding to Redwood. Discussed rollout plan, dedicated vs hosted, VPC options, SSO/SAML, audit logs, initial pilot scope, success metrics, and immediate next steps: share SAML docs, set up staging environment, run baseline perf tests, and schedule technical deep dive with infra team.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-03
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Evelyn (Redwood SE), Laura (SummitCare), Diego, Maya, Tom

Summary (auto): kickoff, onboarding tasks, SSO, pilot scope.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Samir with Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, super excited to kick this off. quick roll call?
[00:06] Laura: hi, Laura here, Head of Platform at SummitCare.
[00:09] Diego: Diego, DevOps.
[00:11] Maya: Maya, security lead.
[00:13] Tom: Tom, CTO.
[00:15] Evelyn: Evelyn, Solutions Engineer at Redwood, I'll be running the tech bits.
[00:20] Samir: Great, agenda for today is quick intros, desired timeline and success criteria, discuss deployment options -- hosted vs dedicated vs private, go over SSO and compliance asks, and agree next steps.
[00:30] Laura: that's perfect. our timeline is kinda tight, we want a pilot in production-ish by end of Q3, so about 12 weeks. success metric is 99th pctl latency under 300ms for chat surface and cost per 1k requests under X threshold, obviously we need cost estimates.
[00:48] Samir: got it, target is end Q3. we'll map pilot SOW to that. on latency/cost we'll give both hosted and dedicated estimates, and some quantization options to reduce cost.
[01:05] Diego: quick question — for dedicated, how do you handle isolation? do we get VPC peering or private link?
[01:12] Evelyn: yeah for Dedicated and Private we offer VPC options. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with VPC peering, Private gives you a customer-managed control plane, can be on-prem or in your VPC. There might be slight variance in latency depending on placement but isolation's strong.
[01:30] Maya: from security perspective we need SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and KMS integration for key wrap. what's out-of-the-box?
[01:42] Evelyn: SAML SSO is supported, RBAC with roles, audit logs and retention can be configured; we integrate with common KMS providers. I'll share our security pack and SOC2 summary after.
[01:55] Samir: we'll attach the SOC2 and SOC2 type II summary. note that some product names in docs might show as Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private but I'll send a single doc with TL;DR.
[02:12] Tom: Very important for us is data residency — some PHI must remain in our region, can Redwood guarantee region pinning?
[02:22] Evelyn: For hosted we have region controls and can pin to a region, for Private you control the infra. We can document region SLA. For Dedicated we can place capacity in your preferred region depending on availability.
[02:38] Laura: what about model updates and rollouts? we want control over model versions and immediate rollback capability.
[02:45] Evelyn: you can pin model versions per route, and we support canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies if a variant fails. the console provides per-route dashboards and latency/cost breakdown.
[03:05] Diego: on the networking piece, who sets up peering — us or Redwood? what's the standard?
[03:12] Evelyn: usually Redwood sets up the endpoint and we work with your network team to accept peering. we'll provide a network runbook. I'll need contact and IP ranges.
[03:26] Laura: we'll provide network contacts after this call.
[03:30] Samir: perfect. next, pilot scope — initial workload is clinical note generation and internal summarization for triage, bursty traffic, average sequence lengths ~250 tokens, occasional long sequences up to 1k.
[03:46] Evelyn: for that profile we recommend a mid-sized open model with 8-bit quantization for cost savings; we'll propose a couple model variants and quantization/kv cache settings. caching prefix/KV can really cut token costs for repeat prompts.
[04:05] Maya: can we get a baseline perf test in our staging environment to validate latency numbers?
[04:10] Evelyn: yes, we'll provision a staging project and run a baseline test; we'll need sample prompts and an approximate QPS.
[04:20] Diego: QPS during pilot steady state maybe 4-8 qps, bursts up to 30.
[04:27] Evelyn: noted. that helps with batching configs.
[04:32] Tom: Regarding encryption — at rest and in transit is required. we also need KMS integration to control keys.
[04:39] Samir: Redwood supports TLS in transit and envelope encryption at rest; KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated. Evelyn will share the KMS integration doc.
[04:48] Maya: we also need retention and deletion policies for logs and any PII. can that be customized?
[04:55] Evelyn: retention windows are configurable for audit logs; data retention for user payloads depends on hosting mode — in Private you control retention, in hosted we have configurable retention and can offer no-persist options for some enterprise tiers. I'll follow up with specifics.
[05:10] Laura: sounds good. can you also share the console UI access flow so our product team can poke around?
[05:15] Samir: yes we'll invite them to the staging project with viewer/editor roles. Evelyn will provision.
[05:22] Evelyn: I'll create invites and share link to quickstart playbook: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding-playbook (note: sample link).
[05:32] Diego: great. what about SLOs and SLA? we need uptime guarantees for pilot-critical routes.
[05:40] Samir: Dedicated offers SLA-backed uptime; hosted has SLAs for paid tiers — we'll include SLA language in the SOW.
[05:50] Tom: pricing — we need an estimate for hosted vs dedicated for the projected usage.
[05:55] Samir: we'll send a pricing sheet; initial pricing ballpark in the SOW, with line items for reserved capacity, burst, and optional observe retention add-on.
[06:08] Maya: any compliance docs for FedRAMP or HIPAA?
[06:12] Evelyn: we have HIPAA guidance and a security pack; for FedRAMP you'd need Private deployment and additional compliance work.
[06:20] Laura: ok we'll review HIPAA pack.
[06:24] Samir: next up, operational runbook: Evelyn will own creating a staging project and a test plan, Samir to draft pilot SOW. Diego to provide VPC details and Maya to provide compliance list.
[06:37] Evelyn: i'll also schedule a technical deep dive to look at KV cache behavior and batching, probably 60-90 minutes.
[06:45] Diego: good, invite our infra folks.
[06:48] Samir: anything else?
[06:50] Laura: one ask — can Redwood support feature flags for model routing so we can do gradual rollout per customer segment?
[06:58] Evelyn: yes feature flags per route via the rollout system, we can support percentage-based rollouts and canary rules.
[07:10] Tom: great. last question — who is our ongoing CSM after onboarding?
[07:15] Samir: we'll assign a named CSM; I'll include that in the SOW.
[07:20] Laura: thanks all.
[07:22] Samir: recap of immediate next steps: Samir shares SAML and SOC2, Evelyn provisions staging and shares playbook link, Diego and Maya send infra/compliance details, Samir to send SOW and pricing. Schedule tech deep dive for next week.
[07:40] Evelyn: i'll send calendar invites for the deep dive and staging access.
[07:44] Laura: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[07:46] Tom: thanks.
[07:48] Diego: bye.
[07:50] END TRANSCRIPT

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cache' heard as 'K-V cache' or 'canary' sometimes as 'cannery'), speaker labels approximate. References to docs: onboarding playbook link above; security pack and SOC2 to be attached by Samir.
